lead_headline: Subscriber net +2 today holds March's 1.4/day MTD pace as restaurant tracker adds 2 new leads (43 total active) and foreclosure filings extend four-week deceleration

restaurant.blurb: 2 new leads today push the active roster to 43 total (21 openings, 22 closures/temp closures). Saturday detections: Bad Rabbit Coffee opens RiNo brick-and-mortar in Cole after mobile caravan roots, third California Pizza Kitchen closure signal surfaces at Cherry Creek—25-year tenant finally confirmed shuttered summer 2025. Week's broader sweep spans downtown hospitality layer: Vaultaire launches today as subterranean HiFi listening bar beneath La Forêt on Broadway, Whisk and Willow Bakery cottage operation folds in West Colfax after 1-2 year run. Opening pipeline holds Union Station weight—Fusion by Tinos Kitchen preps Wynkoop launch, Wapos Cantina Englewood fills former El Tepehuan slot in Rosedale. Closure ledger darkens: New Dragon Berkeley Chinese spot ends 13-year tenure, Sawa Mediterranean pivots University location to catering-only. Seven-day split now 21 openings versus 22 closures—first net-negative week since late February.

foreclosure.blurb: 30 new filings this week flat-lines from last Saturday's 30-count—four-week descent from 49-filing late-February peak now plateaued, breaking prior week's 9% decline momentum. 39 auctions scheduled next seven days, aggregate exposure $11.2M. Sole $2M+ property: Arapahoe's South Columbine Circle at $2.24M, followed by Weld's Falcon Drive ($618K) and Arapahoe's Archer Avenue ($526K). Weld County sustains active caseload lead at 391, El Paso trails 375—exurban concentration unchanged. Filing velocity now arrested after month-long slide (49→42→33→30→30), suggesting seasonal floor reached or March auction cycle exhausted. Stalled decline removes downward pressure but offers no recovery signal—volume stuck at 38% below February peak, mirroring March 2025 spring softening pattern. Next week's data critical to assess whether 30-filing baseline holds or April surge ignites.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday closes the 7-day week at 45 across 11 sources—up 13% from prior week's 40, marking third consecutive week above 40-mention baseline. Denver Post claims 38% share (17 citations), Instagram contributes 7 pickups, social platforms combine for 15 total. Saturday lone detection: Colorado Sun's Littwin column on Post layoffs—ironic meta-coverage of NewsGuild partner outlet. Week's notables include oldest-Colorado-hotel ownership change via Facebook, Mediterranean villa listing through Post real estate desk, Cherry Creek demolition Instagram coverage. Google News RSS captures 98% of flow (44 of 45). Four-week trajectory clarifies: launch-week explosion (53 mentions) settled to 48-mention Week 2, now 45 in Week 3 with 40-baseline Week 4—system stabilizing at ~6.4 daily mentions, sustainable earned media velocity without viral decay. Post partnership anchors consistent referral traffic, social amplification layer adds discovery breadth.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +2 yesterday (2 new, 0 canceled) lifts MTD to +19 (+1.4/day), 90-day cumulative to +80. Past seven days deliver +17 net (25 new, 8 canceled)—8.5x improvement over prior week's anemic +2 (22 new, 20 canceled). March's momentum now anchored by two mid-month surges: March 9's +6 spike and March 12's +4 pop, offsetting March 5's −4 cancellation wave. Cancellation rate compressed to 1.1/day this week versus 2.9/day prior—churn containment driving net recovery as much as new acquisition lift. Month's 1.4/day rate edges YTD's 1.2/day benchmark upward, but weekend zero-net Friday-Saturday (Mar 13-14) raises sustainability questions. Fourteen-day pattern: explosive early-month volatility (Mar 2-5 swung +4 to −4) now stabilizing into steadier +1 to +4 daily range. If March holds 1.4/day through month-end, delivers ~22-net finish—modest but directionally positive after Q1's rocky start.
